name: tumor-tcell-showcase
title: Tumor–T-cell Microenvironment (viva-munk port)
lead:
A faithful port of the multiscale agent-based model from Hickey, Agmon, et al.,
"Integrating multiplexed imaging and multiscale modeling identifies tumor phenotype
conversion as a critical component of therapeutic T cell efficacy," Cell Systems 15,
322–338 (2024), doi:10.1016/j.cels.2024.03.004. The original was built in Vivarium and
integrated with CODEX multiplexed tissue imaging of B16-F10 melanoma; here the tumor, T,
and dendritic cells are per-cell process-bigraph processes over diffusing IFNg / tumor-debris
fields, with cell–cell collisions and neighbor detection delegated to viva-munk's pymunk
engine. Every study is run across replicate seeds (mean ± std), and readouts are separated
into those that hold robustly at tractable scale and those that need the paper's full scale.

at_a_glance.role: The paper's headline experiment (ring-seeded, 3 CODEX conditions) + its full figure suite (population/division/death/snapshots/video), paper colors.
Exhausted (PD1+) T-cell fraction rises with the starting PD1+ fraction (robust, 6/6).
Active T cells reliably secrete the IFNg field that drives conversion (robust, 6/6).
Positive net cytotoxicity vs. a matched no-T control (5/6 seeds).
Scaled up (150 cells, 1500 ticks): the paper's efficacy-vs-exhaustion ordering emerges (3/3 seeds).

biological_story:
The paper's central, counter-intuitive finding is that therapeutic T-cell efficacy is
governed less by how many tumor cells the T cells kill than by how fast they CONVERT the
tumor's phenotype. A CD8+ T cell that engages a tumor cell through TCR–MHC-I secretes
interferon-gamma; the cytokine diffuses through the tissue and drives nearby proliferative
(PDL1-, MHC-I-low) tumor cells into an arrested, inflammatory state (PDL1+, MHC-I-high) that
is negative for cell-cycle markers (G0) — it stops dividing. In the paper's model (1,200
tumor cells + 12 T cells, 3 days), T cells that start mostly active (25% PD1+, from ex-vivo
2HC treatment) drive this conversion EARLIER (~18 h) and more strongly than T cells that
start mostly exhausted (75% PD1+), so the tumor is held to ~1,000 cells vs ~3,000 (75% PD1+)
vs ~5,000 (no T cells) at 60 h — even though the two T-cell conditions produce a nearly
IDENTICAL number of kills (~1,300 vs ~1,200 deaths). Meanwhile repeated TCR stimulation
exhausts the T cells (PD1- -> PD1+), lowering their cytokine output; the paper shows that
spatial reprogramming can preserve the active phenotype for continual conversion and killing.
This port reconstructs that loop from composable parts. At tractable scale the fast,
cell-intrinsic steps — IFNg secretion and T-cell exhaustion — reproduce cleanly across
seeds; and when scaled up the population signature (active T cells suppress growth more than
exhausted ones, via conversion) emerges as in the paper.
question:
Does the process-bigraph port of the tumor-tcell ABM — with viva-munk providing the
collision physics — reproduce the paper's mechanism, and which parts of that mechanism
hold robustly at a tractable scale (tens of cells, tens of simulated hours)?
hypothesis:
Active (PD1-) T cells in contact with tumor cells secrete IFNg and cytotoxic packets.
IFNg diffuses and drives proliferative PDL1n tumors toward the arrested PDL1p state;
cumulative cytotoxic delivery kills tumor cells; and T cells that engage too long become
exhausted (PD1+) and secrete less. The T-cell-intrinsic and cytokine steps should hold at
reduced scale; the slower population-level killing/conversion effects may need paper scale.

acceptance_criteria.behavior: The headline experiment reproduces tumor-tcell's full analysis figure suite (population/division/death/snapshots/video) with the paper's colors.
Exhausted (PD1+) fraction with 75% PD1+ start exceeds 25% PD1+ start (mean over seeds).
Active T cells secrete a measurable IFNg field in every seed; none without T cells.
Mean cytotoxicity (net tumor reduction vs control) is positive across seeds.
At 150 cells/1500 ticks, active (25% PD1+) T cells suppress tumor growth more than exhausted (75% PD1+) in every seed.

executive.what_is_this:
Three replicate-seeded studies exercising the ported microenvironment: T-cell exhaustion
vs. starting PD1+ fraction, IFNg secretion (and conversion), and an in-vitro-style
killing/cytotoxicity assay — each with a mean±std population time-series and a spatial
animation.
executive.verdict: The cell + cytokine mechanisms reproduce robustly across seeds at tractable scale; and when scaled up (150 cells, 1500 ticks) the paper's population efficacy ordering — active T cells suppress tumors more than exhausted ones — emerges in 3/3 seeds. Full paper-scale (1200 cells, 3 days) would tighten the quantitative claim.
decisions_needed: Run the headline conditions at full paper scale (1200 cells, 3 days) on the mini to tighten the ~9% suppression estimate (a tens-of-hours, multi-GB job)?
Promote the robust behaviors (exhaustion, IFNg secretion, positive cytotoxicity, efficacy ordering at scale) to hard gates?

scientific_argument.main_claim:
The viva-munk-physics port recovers the paper's mechanism: active T cells reliably secrete
IFNg (the driver of tumor phenotype conversion), exhaustion accumulates in proportion to
the starting PD1+ fraction, co-culture produces net killing, and — at scale — T cells that
start more active (25% PD1+) suppress tumor growth more than exhausted ones (75% PD1+). As
in the paper, this efficacy difference tracks the RATE of IFNg-driven PDL1n->PDL1p tumor
conversion, not the raw number of kills.
evidence_for: Active T cells secrete a measurable IFNg field in 6/6 seeds; none without T cells.
Exhausted (PD1+) T-cell fraction is higher when seeded with more PD1+ cells in 6/6 seeds (75% start ~63% end vs 25% start ~16% end).
Killing assay: mean cytotoxicity vs. matched no-T control is positive (~11% ± 8%, positive in 5/6 seeds).

AT SCALE (150 cells, 1500 ticks): active (25% PD1+) T cells suppress tumor growth more than exhausted (75% PD1+) in 3/3 seeds (suppression +8.7% vs -7.0%), with PDL1p conversion 14-42% vs 5-9% vs 3-5% (no-T).
evidence_against: At the tractable scale (40 cells, 600 ticks) the tumor-count efficacy ordering and the PDL1p conversion fraction do NOT separate from growth noise (3/6 and 2/6) — they emerge only when scaled up (see efficacy-at-scale).
The scale run is 3 seeds at an intermediate size (150 cells / 25 h), not the paper's full 1200 cells / 3 days; the ~9% suppression magnitude has wide variance.
key_figures: tcell-exhaustion: PD1+ T-cell fraction over time, 25% vs 75% start (mean ± std).
phenotype-conversion: IFNg field over time, with vs without T cells (mean ± std).
killing-assay-cytotoxicity: tumor count over time, +T vs control (mean ± std).
caveats: Scale/time reduced for tractability (40 tumors, 12 T cells, ~10 h). Slow population effects (net suppression, conversion fraction) need paper scale (1200 cells, 3 days) to become significant.

studies.name: tumor-microenvironment
studies.title: Tumor microenvironment (headline experiment) + full figure suite
studies.question:
Does the ported model reproduce tumor-tcell's headline experiment
(tumor_microenvironment_experiment, id '5') — a central tumor mass ringed by
T cells under the three CODEX conditions — and its full analysis figure suite?

studies.name: tcell-exhaustion
studies.title: T-cell exhaustion vs. starting PD1+ fraction
studies.question:
Does the exhausted (PD1+) T-cell fraction over time depend on the fraction of T cells
seeded as exhausted, and is that dependence robust across seeds?

studies.name: phenotype-conversion
studies.title: IFNg secretion and PDL1n->PDL1p conversion
studies.question:
Do active T cells reliably produce the IFNg field that drives tumor phenotype conversion,
and does the downstream PDL1n->PDL1p conversion itself hold at this scale?

studies.name: killing-assay-cytotoxicity
studies.title: In-vitro-style killing / cytotoxicity assay
studies.question:
In a well-mixed assay, do active T cells produce net tumor cell death (positive
cytotoxicity) relative to a matched no-T control, robustly across seeds?

studies.name: efficacy-at-scale
studies.title: T-cell efficacy vs. PD1+ fraction, at larger scale
studies.question:
Does the paper's efficacy-vs-exhaustion ordering — active (25% PD1+) T cells suppress
tumor growth more than exhausted (75% PD1+) T cells — emerge when the simulation is scaled
up from the tractable 40-cell / 600-tick studies?
